short_title: DARC transcytoses intact CCL2/CXCL8 and promotes leukocyte emigration
species_models: Ex vivo human skin venules; engineered polarized MDCK-DARC and immortalized HUVEC-DARC monolayers; endothelial DARC transgenic mice; not healthy or stroke human BBB
molecule_format: 125I-CCL2, 125I-CXCL8 (IL-8), negative ligand 125I-CCL19, endogenous DARC, D6/ACKR2 comparator; full-length chemokines rather than 20-aa engineered peptides
main_endpoint: Direction-resolved transwell chemokine trafficking; intactness by TCA precipitation + CCL2 autoradiography; endothelial ultrastructure; in vivo inflammatory-cell recruitment
receptor_specificity: DARC transfection versus mock, D6 positive degradation comparator, noncognate CCL19, filter reversal, monolayer inulin/TEER; confers ligand-specific reverse-direction transcytosis
luminal_access: DARC localized on luminal and abluminal membrane of human skin venules ex vivo after CXCL8 injection; human brain/stroke blood-facing abundance NOT measured
internalization_trafficking: Ligand-induced CCL2/ACKR1 vesicular trafficking and apical microvillus presentation; caveolin-associated compartments; little degradation vs D6
directional_bbb_delivery: YES: basolateral (tissue) -> apical (blood) chemokine passage in MDCK and engineered HUVEC; NO DARC-enhanced apical/blood -> basolateral/brain transport for CCL2 in either model
intact_cargo_recovery: Intact (TCA-precipitable and autoradiographic) receptor-associated CCL2 demonstrated after basolateral->apical passage; substantial cargo remains bound to apical surface (not freely released). No intact peptide delivered brainward.
quantitative_results: Fig3: intact CCL2 basal->apical increases at 3 h P=0.0005 and 16 h P=0.003; apical->basal no enhancement; chemokine-induced monocyte migration 1.6-fold standard vs 4.3-fold manual flow conditions; in vivo inflammatory reactions enhanced
safety_mechanism: ACKR1-bound chemokines support monocyte/neutrophil extravasation; excess endothelial DARC enhances inflammation; Duffy RBC chemokine reservoir/sink and human erythroid-silent allele acknowledged (discussion).
strengths: Orthogonal ultrastructure, ligand specificity, dual polarized models, biochemical intactness, direction-reversal control, matched membrane integrity markers and in vivo functionality
limitations: Transfected MDCK/HUVEC not brain endothelium; no ischemic models; direction is fundamentally opposite to proposed blood->brain shuttle; chemokine length/structure unlike short peptides; original supplementary figures not supplied
figures_tables: PDF pp2-6; Figs 1-8, especially Fig3(a-d), Fig5(a-c), Fig6-8, Supplementary Fig3/4 cited but not included
evidence_grade: DIRECT ligand-specific intact reverse-direction transport / NEGATIVE evidence for tested apical-to-basal transport / NO short-peptide shuttle

short_title: Inflammatory ACKR1 exports CCL2/CCL5 from abluminal to luminal side of BBB
species_models: Wild-type and Ackr1/Darc-null C57BL/6 and SJL EAE mice; primary mouse brain microvascular endothelial cells (pMBMECs); nine human MS cases vs five controls; reciprocal bone marrow chimeras
molecule_format: Native endothelial ACKR1; recombinant full-length CCL2 and CCL5 (CCL21 nonbinding, CXCL1 nontransported); TNF-alpha, 3/10 kDa dextran, erythrocyte chemokine reservoir
main_endpoint: Inflamed brain vessel protein/RNA induction, direction-resolved lower->upper primary BBB transwells with ELISA, barrier controls, EAE outcomes and compartment-specific chimera effects
receptor_specificity: Darc-null primary endothelial cells vs WT with/without TNF; CCL21 and CXCL1 ligand comparators; 3/10 kDa dextran leak controls; reciprocal bone-marrow chimeras isolate vascular vs erythroid compartments
luminal_access: DARC staining in PECAM1+ EAE inflamed CNS venules from day 7 and higher number of DARC+ human MS brain microvessels than healthy controls; no human stroke luminal epitope quantification or normal brain capillary proof
internalization_trafficking: Cell surface DARC increases after TNF; chemokine binding and transcellular passage inferred; intracellular route not directly traced with specific organelle markers in native pMBMECs
directional_bbb_delivery: YES: CCL2/CCL5 from BRAIN/abluminal -> BLOOD/luminal side in TNF-stimulated primary mouse BBB monolayer, Ackr1-dependent. Apical->basolateral route not tested, not established.
intact_cargo_recovery: ELISA on receiver media reports immunoreactive full-length recombinant chemokines, but no orthogonal LC-MS or sequence-level verification of intact transported ligands; no peptide/cargo blood->brain delivery
quantitative_results: pMBMEC TNF: ~5-6 fold ACKR1 RNA induction; CCL2 and CCL5 reverse flux enhanced in WT, no corresponding enhancement in KO (Fig5); human MS white matter DARC+ vessels higher P=0.0282 (Fig3); barrier 10-kDa dextran nonsignificant WT vs KO
safety_mechanism: Endothelial ACKR1 potentiates leukocyte recruitment and EAE progression; KO attenuates disease; erythrocyte DARC controls circulating CXCL1 reservoir and not the same as vascular ACKR1-mediated BBB effects
strengths: Source-primary BBB model, WT/KO, tightness controls, disease-state staining, human inflammatory brain tissue, two mouse strains and receptor-compartment chimeras
limitations: Autoimmune inflammation (EAE/MS), NOT ischemic stroke; chemokines move brain->blood; human postmortem MS != human stroke; vessel subsets not universal capillaries; no chemical proof of intact receiver ligand; no blood->brain peptide assay; some small cohorts
figures_tables: PDF pp5-13; Figs1-9 (Fig3 human tissue, Fig4 BBB controls, Fig5 transwell, Fig8 RBC reservoir, Fig9 chimeras)
evidence_grade: DIRECT native brain endothelial reverse BBB chemokine transport / HUMAN MS vessel protein evidence / NO blood-to-brain peptide proof

short_title: Cryo-EM of human ACKR1-CCL7 shows shallow CRS1 binding and atypical transducer architecture
species_models: Recombinant purified full-length human ACKR1/CCL7 complex; HEK293 transfection and phosphorylation/interactome assays; not polarized brain EC or human stroke cells
molecule_format: Full-length human 7TM ACKR1; CCL7 (~chemokine protein) and Nb52 nanobody; transducer assays Gi/Gs/Gq, GRK2/3/5/6 and beta-arrestin; structural 8JPS
main_endpoint: CCL7 binding by biochemistry and 3.65-A cryo-EM PDB 8JPS; extracellular residue contacts, signaling tests, phosphoproteomics/interactome; not membrane transport
receptor_specificity: Direct CCL7-purified ACKR1 binding and cryo-EM, mock/chemokine receptor controls for transducer coupling; Nb52 binding separately verified but density not resolved in final map
luminal_access: Predicted and observed extracellular N-terminus (resolved segment ~Glu46-Leu57) accessible to CCL7 in purified receptor; NOT native endothelial luminal display or accessibility under stroke; proximal N-terminus unresolved
internalization_trafficking: No directional cell transport measured. PDB and potential noncanonical partners (CD82, Rab11-related proteins) offer modeling hypotheses, NOT verified ACKR1-mediated BBB transcytosis machinery in human EC
directional_bbb_delivery: NOT TESTED: neither apical-to-basolateral nor basolateral-to-apical chemokine/peptide flux. 3D binding is not evidence of blood-to-brain delivery.
intact_cargo_recovery: Not tested; structural complex with CCL7 and 7TM receptor, no transported cargo recovery
quantitative_results: Cryo-EM map 3.65 A; PDB 8JPS; DARC Glu46-Asn55 N-terminal contact (Glu46-Leu57 loop), Cys51-Cys276(7.25) disulfide; little/no CRS2 pocket engagement; ~8,215 phosphopeptides / >2,600 proteins, ~300 differential protein hits; ~1,700 interactors and 73 regulated interactions
safety_mechanism: Chemokine promiscuity and pathogen/toxin engagement at N terminus; noncanonical signaling remains possible despite absence of canonical G-protein/GRK/beta-arrestin coupling; widespread erythrocyte antigen and peripheral endothelium
strengths: Reproducible structural and orthogonal assay panels, published 8JPS model and map, disulfide-defined epitope, noncanonical partner discovery, direct binding of CCL7
limitations: No receptor-specific peptide design/delivery. Proximal N terminus absent in structural coordinates; dimer arrangement may be nonphysiological; Nb52 density absent; purification/posttranslational settings differ from human BBB; 3.65 A limited side-chain precision; phosphoproteomic association is not mechanism proof; supplemental Data S1/Tables S1-S5 not included in this PDF
figures_tables: PDF pp1-15 Figs1-7; pp16-45 methods and reporting; PDB 8JPS (doi:10.2210/pdb8JPS/pdb); missing online supplemental Data S1 and Tables S1-S5
evidence_grade: DIRECT human receptor structure and ligand interface / NO transport evidence / exploratory noncanonical signaling
